subject: Operations
title: Push vs. Pull Supply Chains
description: Learn Push vs. Pull Supply Chains in one minute.

hook.text: A factory makes 10,000 umbrellas before summer. Nobody buys them. That's push gone wrong.

buildup.text: Push systems produce based on forecasts. Pull systems produce based on actual customer demand.

discovery.text: Push risks overproduction. Pull risks being too slow. Many chains blend both with a decoupling point.

twist.text: Dell pioneered pull: no laptop was built until a customer ordered it. This eliminated finished goods inventory.

climax.text: The decoupling point is where push meets pull—upstream is forecast-driven, downstream is demand-driven.

punchline.text: Push to predict. Pull to respond. Blend to win.

quiz.question: What is a pull supply chain driven by?
